source.title: Across the Loss Landscape with Progressive Growth
source.authors: Paul Caillon; Christophe Cerisara; Alexandre Allauzen

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares progressive parameter growth with full-model training and reports test accuracy and geometric measures, but does not test any listed version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-100 test accuracy for growth schedules and controls, alongside transition barriers, retention, and restricted-curvature ratios. It does not report a train–test gap, fitting random labels, widening past an interpolation threshold, or magnitude-aware sharpness. Its curvature and transition measures therefore do not test V7 as stated. The MLP experiment is on two-moons, not natural image labels, and is not extracted as a row.
record.test_reason: The study tests progressive parameter release and transition geometry, not any listed claim version. Its restricted Hessian eigenvalue ratios compare newly released with already active directions; they do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or rank train–test gaps as V7 requires. Parameter release is not a width sweep beyond interpolation, and optimizer, batch size, dropout, architecture type and example removal are not experimentally compared.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, progressive constraint relaxation biases basin accessibility through initialization proximity and frozen-direction curvature. Toy experiments show that proximity can reverse the flatness preference. In ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, progressive growth yields relatively low-curvature newly released directions and schedule-dependent transition stability, but lower test accuracy than full-model training. These results do not establish a universal flatness–generalization relationship.
record.recipe_differences: Studies progressive parameter release and transition geometry; it does not reproduce the claim's listed random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch, dropout, sharpness-gap, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Growth trigger and stage count change transition barriers and retention; patience changes barrier more noticeably than final test accuracy. Newly released subspace curvature ratios also vary by schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: All progressive ResNet-18 growth schedules score below full-model training on CIFAR-100: 73.37–75.54% versus 76.25%. Their newly released-to-active restricted curvature ratios range from 0.0859 to 0.313.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Progressive parameter release can expose relatively low-curvature directions without improving held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed-subspace training reaches 3.13% accuracy; one-shot unfreezing reaches 75.84% with curvature ratio 0.7913, versus 0.201 for five-stage validation-triggered growth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradual constraint relaxation produces a different released-direction curvature signature from delayed one-shot capacity release.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation-triggered growth retains low barriers across stage counts; training-loss-triggered growth has zero mean barrier at three stages but barriers of 0.1247 and 0.1442 at five and ten stages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The stability of progressive parameter-release transitions depends on trigger and stage count.

record.problems: Deep-learning evidence covers one architecture family and one dataset; results are averaged over 3 seeds. Transition losses use at most 2 validation batches, and restricted Hessian estimates use a single non-augmented training batch. The study does not report train–test gaps or test the listed claim versions directly.
record.rows_left_out: The two-moons MLP experiment in Appendix B.10 and patience-ablation plot in Figure 2 are not extracted: the MLP uses a synthetic task rather than natural labels, and the patience results are figure-only without text-stated values for each condition. Toy landscape basin-selection results are also omitted because they are synthetic quadratic basins rather than trained neural networks on natural data.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out performance.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity or initialization comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning, switching, and decoupled weight decay.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with train–test gaps at comparable training loss, and its ranking against norm and margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. All recorded numbers match the supplied tables, but the rows concern the study's own method and controls and belong only under fits_no_version. The two-moons MLP experiment also tests none of V1–V8; its exclusion is not justified merely by synthetic data. No omitted result bears on a listed version. The abstract states that code is available on GitHub, contrary to the record's code_released field.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label performance in the listed architectures and settings.
Width sweep beyond zero training error for one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the specified local-connectivity comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and the stated tuning, decay, and switching conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and the specified recipe adaptations.
Dropout additions and removals under the stated training-set and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, its ranking of train–test gaps, and comparisons with the named norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and comparison with random-example removal.
